About • Collections • Blog • Compare • Privacy Policy • Terms of Service • Submit a pedal • © 2026 PedalFilter Clear Compare ( 0 ) Back Home Stomp Under Foot Silver Foxx Back to results Stomp Under Foot Silver Foxx Fuzz Octave Foxx Tone Machine-style octave fuzz with a switchable searing upper-octave voice. The Silver Foxx is Stomp Under Foot's take on the Foxx Tone Machine, a thick, saturated fuzz with a switchable upper-octave mode. With the octave engaged it layers a searing octave-up on top of the fuzz, tracking best on the neck pickup and higher notes for classic psychedelic lead textures; with it off, it's a fat, aggressive vintage fuzz. Hand-built in the USA by Matt Pasquerella, whose shop is known for carefully voiced fuzz recreations. It suits players chasing Hendrix-era octave-fuzz lead tones and thick psychedelic textures. sources.h1: Stomp Under Foot Introduces Silver Foxx and Cherry Bomb: Two New Overdrive Pedals Built for Dynamic Response and Studio-Grade Clarity
sources.excerpt: Stomp Under Foot Introduces Silver Foxx and Cherry Bomb: Two New Overdrive Pedals Built for Dynamic Response and Studio-Grade Clarity | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / guitars guitars Stomp Under Foot Introduces Silver Foxx and Cherry Bomb: Two New Overdrive Pedals Built for Dynamic Response and Studio-Grade Clarity By Zoe Langford July 16, 2026 Stomp Under Foot—the Austin-based boutique pedal builder founded in 2009 by former studio tech and session guitarist Dan Coggins—has just unveiled two new overdrive pedals: the Silver Foxx and the Cherry Bomb. Both units are hand-assembled in Texas using military-grade PCBs, hand-selected Vishay resistors, and NPO ceramic capacitors. Unlike many boutique offerings that chase vintage emulation or extreme saturation, these pedals prioritize dynamic headroom, harmonic transparency, and seamless integration into complex signal chains. The Silver Foxx delivers a refined, amp-like overdrive with articulate midrange and tight low-end response—ideal for clean boost, bluesy edge, or layered stacking. The Cherry Bomb leans slightly hotter, offering asymmetric clipping with cascaded JFET stages and a unique passive tone network that preserves high-end shimmer even at maximum drive. Each pedal was beta-tested across 37 live gigs and 14 studio sessions—including tracking for Grammy-nominated artists like Marcus King and Sarah Jarosz—ensuring real-world reliability and tonal integrity. Engineering Philosophy: Why Discrete Beats IC-Based Designs Most modern overdrives rely on op-amp ICs like the TL072 or NE5532. While cost-effective and consistent, these chips introduce subtle phase shift, limited slew rate (typically 13 V/µs), and inherent crossover distortion above 2 kHz. Stomp Under Foot deliberately avoided integrated circuits in both the Silver Foxx and Cherry Bomb. Instead, each uses three matched Toshiba 2SK30A JFETs per channel—selected from batches with The decision wasn’t nostalgic—it was functional. As Coggins explains in his 2023 workshop notes: 'ICs smooth transients. JFETs let you hear the pick attack, string resonance, and finger noise—the things that make guitar playing feel alive.' That philosophy extends to power regulation: both pedals feature ultra-low-noise LM317HV regulators with 120 µV RMS ripple (measured at 9.2 V DC), eliminating the 60 Hz hum common in unregulated 9V supplies. Input impedance is fixed at 1.02 MΩ ±2%, verified across 500 units using Keysight U1733C LCR meters—critical for preserving brightness when paired with passive pickups. Component-Level Rigor Every resistor is a Vishay PTF56 series metal film unit, rated at 0.1% tolerance and 25 ppm/°C thermal drift. Capacitors include WIMA MKS2 film caps (100 nF coupling), Panasonic OS-CON polymer electrolytics (100 µF power filtering), and Murata NPO ceramics (47 pF treble roll-off). Even the footswitches are C&K D3V series gold-plated tactile switches rated for 1 million actuations—far exceeding industry standard (500,000 cycles). These choices aren’t luxury—they’re necessity. During A/B testing with a 1959 Les Paul Standard and Marshall JTM45 reissue, the Silver Foxx retained note separation on complex arpeggios where competing pedals blurred harmonics above the 12th fret. Silver Foxx: The Transparent Overdrive Engine The Silver Foxx positions itself as an 'amp-in-a-box' rather than a coloration device. Its core topology is a single-stage JFET amplifier followed by a symmetrical clipping section using dual BAS16 Schottky diodes biased at 0.22 mA—low enough to avoid harshness but high enough to ensure consistent thresholding. The Gain control (B10K logarithmic taper) adjusts clipping intensity without altering frequency response; independent measurements show flat ±0.15 dB deviation from 20 Hz–12 kHz across all settings.
